content:
Let \(d\) be the working days per week.

Initial work:  
\[
180 \times 8 \times 10d = 14400d
\]
man-hours completed \(3\) km, so \(12\) km remaining requires  
\[
4 \times 14400d = 57600d
\]
man-hours.

In the remaining \(30\) weeks, men work \(9\) hours/day:
\[
180 \times 9 \times 30d = 48600d
\]
man-hours.

Let \(x\) boys be employed. Since \(3\) boys \(=2\) men, each boy’s work is \(\frac23\) of a man’s. If boys also work \(9\) hours/day:
\[
x \times 9 \times 30d \times \frac23 = 180xd
\]
equivalent man-hours.

So,
\[
48600d + 180xd = 57600d
\]
\[
180x = 9000
\]
\[
x = 50
\]

\[
\boxed{50}
\]
